extracted.intended_audience: FCC program administrators, the designated SDO, Office of General Counsel, bureau/office staff, regulated program participants (service providers, resellers, beneficiaries), and legal/compliance advisors
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules governing suspension, debarment, exceptions, transitions, reciprocity, alternative remedies, and related processes for participants in FCC programs (e.g., Lifeline, E-Rate, RHC, TRS, NDBEDP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions subject to oversight conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any exceptions shall be subject to appropriate conditions such as mandatory audits, additional reporting requirements, compliance agreements (with approval of OGC), monitoring, or any other forms of effective oversight supplemental to those already provided under FCC programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions may be conditioned on administrative agreements and oversight to protect program integrity; OGC approval is required for compliance agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of alternate providers as factor for exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The availability of alternate service providers to serve customers and end-users in a given area is one relevant factor for the Commission to consider in deciding whether to grant an exception to Commission exclusions or to those issued by another agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a participant contends it is sole provider, the SDO must afford the administering bureau an opportunity to rebut; SDO should evaluate geographic availability of alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDO coordination with bureaus to rebut sole-provider claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If a participant contends that it is the sole provider of services, the SDO shall afford the bureau that administers the program involved an opportunity to address this matter and rebut those assertions if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureaus/offsices provide subject-matter input on market/provider availability when SDO evaluates exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption to require beneficiaries to transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a presumption that the SDO require beneficiaries receiving services from an excluded provider to transition to new providers, subject to limited exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation policies in sections 180.310/180.315 are not applied to these programs; SDO should ensure beneficiaries secure alternate providers promptly to maintain program integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: No indefinite continuation for month-to-month services
rubrics_metrics.description: Many Lifeline consumers receive service on a month-to-month basis; treating such relationships as long-term contracts would allow excluded providers to continue indefinitely, which is unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SDo must prevent excluded providers from providing indefinite services simply because contracts are short-term; require transitions where alternatives exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDO authority to fashion reasonable transition periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The SDO is authorized to fashion reasonable transition periods that protect beneficiaries from loss of services and to grant exceptions pursuant to Supplemental Rule 6001.125 subject to administrative agreements and agency oversight as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transition periods should balance protecting program integrity with avoiding service disruption; may include compliance agreements and enhanced oversight; OGC approval required for compliance agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to remove excluded persons from roles
rubrics_metrics.description: An exclusion would require that the organization remove those excluded persons from any role and duties in covered transactions (including oversight responsibilities) and transfer their duties for such transactions to other individuals as may be needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations must reassign or replace excluded officers, directors, program managers to prevent continued participation by bad actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of underlying carriers as alternatives for resellers
rubrics_metrics.description: For participants who are resellers, there will almost always be alternative sources because resellers purchase services or equipment from underlying carriers or manufacturers who may continue providing services to customers and end-users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SDo should consider underlying carriers as natural transition targets for beneficiaries of resellers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate cessation for marketing/enrollment/consulting entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The SDO shall require that marketing organizations, enrollment representatives, or consultants who have been suspended or debarred immediately cease their operations related to covered transactions; no exceptions or transitional periods shall be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program participants cannot continue doing business with such marketing/consulting entities during suspension/debarment; immediate discontinuation prevents excluded actors from benefiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for programs with single certified providers (NDBEDP/TRS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because state NDBEDP/TRS programs may contract with a single provider for a jurisdiction, suspended or debarred providers may need to continue to provide services with appropriate safeguards until another entity is certified or contracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CGB should request voluntary relinquishment of certification; Commission will expedite certification review and follow notice/hearing procedures for revocation; SDO may permit limited continuations with safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited certification and revocation procedures for TRS/NDBEDP
rubrics_metrics.description: If a TRS or NDBEDP contractor is suspended or debarred and is the only provider in a jurisdiction, the Commission will expedite certification of alternatives and follow its notice and hearing process for suspending or revoking certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures exclusions are implemented consistent with Commission rules while safeguarding beneficiaries' needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDo must evaluate services, alternatives, contract terms, and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: To achieve transition goals, the SDO must closely evaluate the particular services provided, the availability of alternate providers in the geographic areas served, the typical terms of any contracts, and any federal or state certification requirements applicable in programs like NDBEDP or TRS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation informs whether a continuation is necessary and the appropriate transitional order or administrative agreement to ensure expedited transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded providers to continue services during transition consistent with rules
rubrics_metrics.description: During any transitional period, the excluded providers shall continue providing services to their beneficiaries consistent with our rules and with their contractual obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SDO must ensure transitions do not violate program rules; if obtaining alternative providers requires bidding or certifications, transition must allow sufficient time for that process.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDO may permit limited extended continuations in extraordinary situations
rubrics_metrics.description: In extraordinary situations where alternative providers cannot be identified as quickly as anticipated, the SDO may permit a continuation beyond the initial transition period, but any extended transition should be limited and as short as feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SDo should set finite duration and require excluded providers to send timely notices to customers of the need to transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer notice requirements for transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices to affected customers or end-users should include: (1) a statement that the participating provider has been suspended or debarred; (2) a statement that the provider will continue to provide services until the date certain as specified in the suspension or debarment order; (3) a statement that users should obtain service from another provider; and (4) a listing of names and contact information for other providers authorized to supply that service in the jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SDo shall require excluded providers to send these timely notices; consider prior transition/notice provisions (especially for Lifeline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency reciprocity generally adopted with exception procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities excluded by other federal agencies' SDOs will be excluded from the Commission's nonprocurement programs, but the Commission adopts supplemental rules allowing petitions for exceptions to reciprocity evaluated by the SDO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities must notify the Commission promptly; the SDO will conduct a preliminary review and may entertain exception petitions under Supplemental Rules 6001.120(d) and 6001.125.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification deadlines for exclusions by other agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: FCC program participants or principals excluded by another agency must promptly notify the Commission within ten business days after receiving notice of the exclusion; participants/principals already included in SAM.gov Exclusion based on conduct before effective date must notify within 30 days after rules become effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications to be made by email and letter to bureau/office heads, program administrators, General Counsel, and Managing Director; OGC may revise methods where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary continuation of existing transactions but no new transactions pending exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants or principals excluded by other agencies may temporarily continue with existing covered transactions under FCC programs but may not enter into new transactions unless an exception is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They must comply with any SDO-ordered transitions or limited continuations; barred from enrolling new customers or entering new covered transactions if no exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step exception procedure for reciprocity (preliminary review + exception determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure consists of a preliminary review by the SDO and the SDO's subsequent exception determination, if warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary evaluation factors include timing of misconduct, timing of other agency's exclusion, sole-source status, and remaining duration; SDO consults OGC and administering bureaus; if no exception, informal transition proceedings commence and excluded party has 30 days to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for granting exceptions to reciprocity
rubrics_metrics.description: The SDO may grant an exception only if doing so is supported by a preponderance of the evidence, and exceptions should be granted only infrequently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions may be conditioned on audits, reporting, compliance agreements (OGC approval), monitoring, or other oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAM.gov registration requirement after exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: A participant that is not already registered with SAM.gov must do so within 10 days of the date that its suspension or debarment becomes effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing differs between suspension (effective when first imposed) and debarment (effective only when SDO issues final decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: SDO authority to use alternative remedies/administrative agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: The SDO has authority to fashion settlements (administrative agreements) short of imposing exclusions, including compliance agreements, as alternative remedies under sections 180.635 and 180.650 of the Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SDO must consult and coordinate with OGC in structuring administrative agreements and obtain OGC approval; agreements may not impede recovery of improper payments or resolve other government claims without appropriate participation/approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on administrative agreements and global settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative agreements may not (i) impede or impair the Commission's authority to seek full recovery under its debt collection authority of any improper payments; or (ii) purport to resolve any claims the Government may have against the settling party. Global settlements require participation and approval of all relevant decisionmakers (Commission, DOJ, other agencies) as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects government's ability to pursue other remedies and claim recoveries despite administrative settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors favoring administrative agreements (self-reporting, remediation, monitoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: One factor that could weigh in favor of resolution through an administrative agreement is a participant's self-reporting of an issue, depending on severity and whether it was reported promptly and remediated; effective agreements often require training, compliance obligations, reporting, auditing, and/or independent monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of administrative agreements should be case-by-case with monitoring and audit requirements to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard debarment period with flexibility to adjust
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the standard three-year debarment period under section 180.865, with flexibility for the SDO to consider adjustments based on seriousness of causes and factors in the Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debarred persons may petition under sections 180.875/180.880 for reduction based on factors such as absence of alternative service provider or satisfactory post-debarment compliance agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readmission petition requirement for egregious conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule permitting the SDO to determine that a participant's conduct was so egregious as to require it to petition for readmission to Commission programs; petitioner must demonstrate implemented remedial actions to avoid future violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies regardless of change of ownership; failure to file or denial may lead to extension of debarment under section 180.885 to protect public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDO appointment, neutrality, and use of subject-matter expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission will designate an SDO who should be neutral and whose decisions should be informed by relevant subject matter experts within the Commission; SDO will preside over suspension and debarment proceedings under delegated authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission will address organizational needs when making appointment; OGC, OMD, Enforcement Bureau, Wireline Competition Bureau, and CGB to coordinate as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissive use of pre-notice letters
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission permits the use of pre-notice letters (show cause letters, requests for information) to inform individuals/entities that suspension/debarment is being reviewed and give opportunity to respond prior to formal SDO action, but will not require them in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-notice letters are useful where administrative agreement may resolve matter; mandating them could slow needed protective action in egregious cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of permissive imputation of conduct rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the Guidelines' imputation rule, permitting the agency to impute conduct from an individual to an organization, from an organization to an individual, among individuals, or among organizations in appropriate circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imputation is permissive (the agency 'may' impute); SDO should consider facts case-by-case (knowledge, approval, acquiescence, inadequate supervision) and is not limited to strict employment-scope scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of evidence: OIG responsibility when it investigated
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Office of Inspector General (OIG) has conducted the underlying investigation supporting suspension and debarment, it should have primary responsibility for providing the information to the SDO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG expected to supply evidentiary materials because it is most familiar with underlying facts; other evidentiary procedures will be addressed as needed.
